headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/cascading-error from untrusted content, but both docs-only profiles show no shared channel or write surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both profiles show no shared communication channel, no filesystem surface, and network_egress is none for agent_a and agent_b. With no documented bridge, a prompt-injection pathway between spring-integration-samples and system-prompts-leaks is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent begins parsing the other's output as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared workspace.
Do not copy outputs from one agent into the other without review.
Add provenance labels to any transferred text.
requires-engineering: enforce channel-level isolation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither agent reports data_classes_touched, and both have network_egress set to none. With no shared workspace or authenticated principal shown, there is no documented path for spring-integration-samples or system-prompts-leaks to leak data to each other.
conditions: IF either agent is connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk increases.
IF either agent gains outbound network access, reassess exfiltration risk.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Verify both agents remain network-disabled.
Separate credentials and OAuth principals.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on any future shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The profiles expose no write capabilities, no concurrency model, and no shared mutable resource. spring-integration-samples and system-prompts-leaks therefore have no documented overlapping write surface that could conflict.
conditions: IF either agent is granted filesystem, git, or database write access to the same target, conflict risk appears.
IF an orchestrator introduces shared mutable state without locking, reassess.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Avoid placing them on the same writable directory.
Do not let either agent modify git state.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: No downstream action-taking authority is documented, and neither profile shows a channel where one agent's output becomes the other's authoritative input. Without such a pipeline, spring-integration-samples cannot cascade errors into system-prompts-leaks or vice versa.
conditions: IF one agent's output is fed into the other without verification, cascading-error risk becomes plausible.
IF either agent is given authority to send messages or commit actions, reassess.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Do not auto-forward outputs from one agent to the other.
Require explicit verification before any action.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes, residency constraints, certifications, or retention policies are documented for either spring-integration-samples or system-prompts-leaks. With only docs-only profiles and no sensitive-data flow shown, there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF either profile later documents PHI, EU PII, or retention obligations, reassess compliance.
IF the pair is deployed under a regulated workload, verify residency and retention settings.
mitigations: Document the data classes each agent may touch.
Confirm retention settings before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of this pair.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
